title.zh: 卷8 志第3 禮儀三
title.raw: 卷8 志第3 禮儀三 Volume 8 Treatises 3: Rites 3

sentences.zh: 禮儀三

translations.literal: Rites 3
translations.idiomatic: Rites 3

sentences.zh: 陳永定三年七月，武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Yongding of Chen, Emperor Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chen Yongding 3 (559), Emperor Wu passed away.

sentences.zh: 新除尚書左丞庾持稱：「晉、宋以來，皇帝大行儀注，未祖一日，告南郊太廟，奏策奉諡。

translations.literal: The newly appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Yu Chi stated: "Since Jin and Song times, in the rites and regulations for the deceased emperor, before the first day of ancestral rites, they announced to the Southern Suburban Altar and Grand Temple, presented memorials and conferred posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, Yu Chi, said: "Since the Jin and Song dynasties, in the prescribed rites for a deceased emperor's passage, announcement was made at the Southern Suburban Altar and the Grand Temple before the first day of ancestral sacrifice, with memorials submitted to confer the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 梓宮將登轀輬，侍中版奏，已稱某諡皇帝。

translations.literal: When the spirit coffin was about to be placed on the hearse, the Attendant-in-Ordinary announced by tablet, already calling him Emperor with such-and-such posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial coffin was about to be mounted on the funeral carriage, the Attendant-in-Ordinary announced by plaque that he was already styled the Emperor with the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 遣奠，出於陛階下，方以此時，乃讀哀策。

translations.literal: For the send-off offering, going out below the court steps, it was at this time that the lamentation scroll was read.
translations.idiomatic: At the farewell offering below the court steps, the mourning scroll was read at that very moment.

sentences.zh: 而前代策文，猶雲大行皇帝，請明加詳正。

translations.literal: Yet the memorial texts of former ages still say "the late emperor," and he requested clarification and detailed correction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the memorial texts of earlier dynasties still used the phrase "the late emperor," and he asked that this be clearly corrected in detail.

sentences.zh: 」國子博士、領步兵校尉、知儀禮沈文阿等謂：「應劭《風俗通》，前帝諡未定，臣子稱大行，以別嗣主。

translations.literal: " The Director of the Imperial Academy, Concurrent Colonel of the Foot Soldiers, and Supervisor of Ritual and Etiquette Shen Wen'a and others said: "In Ying Shao's Customary Usage, before the former emperor's posthumous title was fixed, ministers and subjects called him "the late emperor" to distinguish him from the succeeding sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Academy, Concurrent Colonel of the Foot Soldiers, and Supervisor of Ritual and Etiquette Shen Wen'a and others replied: "In Ying Shao's Customary Usage, before the deceased emperor's posthumous title was settled, ministers and subjects addressed him as "the late emperor" to distinguish him from the new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 近檢梁儀，自梓宮將登轀輬，版奏皆稱某諡皇帝登轀輬。

translations.literal: On recently checking Liang ritual practice, from when the spirit coffin was about to be placed on the hearse, the tablet announcements all called him Emperor with such-and-such posthumous title mounting the hearse.
translations.idiomatic: On recently examining Liang ritual regulations, from the moment the imperial coffin was to be mounted on the funeral carriage, plaque announcements consistently used the posthumous imperial title in stating that the Emperor mounted the carriage.

sentences.zh: 伏尋今祖祭已奉策諡，哀策既在庭，遣祭不應猶稱大行。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering that now the ancestral rite has already received the conferred posthumous title by memorial, and the lamentation scroll is already in the courtyard, the send-off offering should not still call him "the late emperor."
translations.idiomatic: On reverent inquiry, since the ancestral sacrifice has already been conducted with the posthumous title conferred by memorial, and the mourning scroll is already in the courtyard, the send-off offering should no longer use the term "late emperor."

sentences.zh: 且哀策篆書，藏于玄宮。

translations.literal: Moreover, the lamentation scroll is in seal script and stored in the dark palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the mourning scroll was written in seal script and placed in storage within the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 」謂「依梁儀稱諡，以傳無窮」。

translations.literal: " They said, "Follow Liang ritual and use the posthumous title, so that it may be transmitted without end."
translations.idiomatic: They concluded, "The Liang ritual should be followed and the posthumous title used, so that it may be handed down without end."

sentences.zh: 詔可之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this by edict.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年八月癸亥，尚書儀曹請今月晦皇太后服安吉君禫除儀注。

translations.literal: On the day guihai of the eighth month of the first year of Tianjia, the Ritual Section of the Secretariat requested ritual regulations for the empress dowager's end of mourning service for Lady Anji on the last day of this month.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the eighth month of Tianjia 1 (560), the Ritual Section of the Secretariat requested the prescribed rites for the empress dowager's end of mourning for Lady Anji, to be observed on the last day of that month.

sentences.zh: 沈洙議：「謂至親期斷，加降故再期，而再周之喪，斷二十五月。

translations.literal: Shen Zhu argued: "It is said that for the closest kin the mourning period is cut off, but with added reduction it becomes two periods again, and for mourning of two cycles the period is cut off at twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhu argued: "For the closest kin, the mourning period is terminated at one full cycle, but with the added reduction it becomes two cycles again; mourning of two cycles ends at twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 但重服不可頓除，故變之以纖縞，創巨不可便愈，故稱之以祥禫。

translations.literal: But heavy mourning cannot be removed all at once, so it is changed by fine hempen cloth; a great wound cannot heal immediately, so it is called by the xiang and chan stages.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy mourning cannot be cast off all at once, so it is gradually changed through fine hempen cloth; a great wound cannot heal immediately, so the stages of xiang and chan are used to mark the transition.

sentences.zh: 禫者，淡也，所以漸祛其情。

translations.literal: Chan means fading, by which the emotion is gradually dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: "Chan" means to fade—the term denotes the gradual easing of grief.

sentences.zh: 至如父在為母出適後之子，則屈降之以期。

translations.literal: As for a son born after his mother had left the household while his father was still alive, the mourning is reduced and lowered to one period.
translations.idiomatic: For a son born after his mother had remarried while his father was still alive, mourning is reduced to one full cycle.

sentences.zh: 期而除服，無複衰麻。

translations.literal: At the end of one period the mourning garments are removed, with no further sackcloth or hemp.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of one cycle the mourning garments are removed, with no further sackcloth or hemp.

sentences.zh: 緣情有本同之義，許以心制。

translations.literal: Following the emotion there is a principle of shared origin, and heart-mourning is permitted by inner regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Because grief arises from a shared bond of kinship, heart-mourning is permitted as an inward regulation of feeling.

sentences.zh: 心制既無杖絰可除，不容複改玄'，既是心憂，則無所更淡其心也。

translations.literal: Since heart-mourning has no staff or hempen headband to remove, one cannot again change dark mourning dress; since it is grief of the heart, there is nothing by which to fade the heart further.
translations.idiomatic: Since heart-mourning involves no staff or hempen headband to remove, one cannot again change out of dark mourning dress; as it is grief held in the heart, there is no further stage by which to lighten that grief.

sentences.zh: 且禫杖期者，十五月已有禫制。

translations.literal: Moreover, for chan with staff in one-period mourning, at fifteen months there is already a chan regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for chan mourning with staff in one-period cases, the chan stage already applies at fifteen months.

sentences.zh: 今申其免懷之感，故斷以再周，止二十五月而已。

translations.literal: Now, extending the feeling of longing from the womb, the period is cut off at two cycles, stopping at twenty-five months only.
translations.idiomatic: Now, extending the longing felt from the womb, the period is terminated at two full cycles, ending at twenty-five months only.

sentences.zh: 所以宋元嘉立義，心喪以二十五月為限。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Yuanjia era of Song, the principle was established that heart-mourning is limited to twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in Song Yuanjia, the principle was established that heart-mourning is limited to twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 大明中，王皇后父喪，又申明其制。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, when Empress Wang's father died, this regulation was again clarified.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era, when Empress Wang's father died, this regulation was reaffirmed.

sentences.zh: 齊建元中，太子穆妃喪，亦同用此禮。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era of Qi, when the crown prince's consort Mu died, this same rite was also used.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianyuan, when the crown prince's consort Mu died, this same rite was also applied.

sentences.zh: 唯王儉《古今集記》雲心制終二十七月，又為王逡所難。

translations.literal: Only Wang Jian's Comprehensive Record of Ancient and Modern Matters says heart-mourning ends at twenty-seven months, and this was again challenged by Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Jian's Comprehensive Record of Ancient and Modern Matters states that heart-mourning ends at twenty-seven months, and this was challenged again by Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 何佟之儀注用二十五月而除。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi's ritual regulations use twenty-five months for removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi's ritual regulations prescribe removal of mourning at twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 案古循今，宜以再週二十五月為斷。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity and following the present, the termination should be at two cycles, twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Examining antiquity and following present practice, the termination should be set at two cycles, twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 今皇太后于安吉君心喪之期，宜除于再周，無複心禫之禮。

translations.literal: Now for the empress dowager's heart-mourning period for Lady Anji, mourning should end at two cycles, with no further heart-chan rite.
translations.idiomatic: For the empress dowager's heart-mourning period for Lady Anji, mourning should end at two cycles, with no further heart-chan ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」詔可之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this by edict.

sentences.zh: 隋制，諸嶽崩瀆竭，天子素服，避正寢，撤膳三日。

translations.literal: Under Sui regulations, when mountains collapsed or rivers dried up, the Son of Heaven wore plain white robes, avoided the main palace hall, and withdrew food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui regulations, when mountains collapsed or rivers ran dry, the emperor wore plain white robes, avoided the main palace hall, and abstained from the regular table for three days.

sentences.zh: 遣使祭崩竭之山川，牲用太牢。

translations.literal: Envoys were dispatched to sacrifice at the mountains and rivers that had collapsed or dried up, using a full complement of sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifice at the mountains and rivers that had collapsed or dried up, using the full complement of sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 皇帝本服大功已上親及外祖父母、皇后父母、諸官正一品喪，皇帝不視事三日。

translations.literal: When the emperor himself was in mourning for kin within great mourning and above, or for maternal grandparents, the empress's parents, or officials of the first rank, the emperor did not attend to affairs for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor himself was in mourning for kin within great mourning and above, or for maternal grandparents, the empress's parents, or officials of the first rank, he did not conduct state business for three days.

sentences.zh: 皇帝本服五服內親及嬪、百官正二品已上喪，並一舉哀。

translations.literal: When the emperor himself was in mourning for kin within the five degrees of mourning, or for consorts, or for officials of the second rank and above, there was one session of lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor himself was in mourning for kin within the five degrees of mourning, for consorts, or for officials of the second rank and above, he performed one session of lamentation.

sentences.zh: 太陽虧、國忌日，皇帝本服小功緦麻親、百官三品已上喪，皇帝皆不視事一日。

translations.literal: On a solar eclipse or the anniversary of a national mourning day, when the emperor himself was in mourning for kin in lesser mourning and hempen mourning, or for officials of the third rank and above, the emperor did not attend to affairs for one day.
translations.idiomatic: On a solar eclipse or a national mourning anniversary, when the emperor was in lesser mourning or hempen mourning for close kin, or when officials of the third rank and above were in mourning, the emperor did not conduct state business for one day.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇后為本服五服內諸親及嬪，一舉哀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and empress, for kin within the five degrees of mourning in their own mourning obligations, and for consorts, performed one session of lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and empress, for kin within the five degrees of mourning in their own obligations and for consorts, performed one session of lamentation.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為本服五服之內親及東宮三師、三少、宮臣三品已上，一舉哀。

translations.literal: The crown prince, for kin within the five degrees of mourning in his own obligations and for the Eastern Palace's three preceptors, three junior tutors, and palace officials of the third rank and above, performed one session of lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, for kin within the five degrees of mourning in his own obligations and for the Eastern Palace's three preceptors, three junior tutors, and palace officials of the third rank and above, performed one session of lamentation.

sentences.zh: 又二年，始興王嗣子喪。

translations.literal: Also in the second year, the heir of the Prince of Shixing died.
translations.idiomatic: Also in the second year, the heir of the Prince of Shixing died.

sentences.zh: 博士管晅議，使國長從服緦麻。

translations.literal: Doctor Guan Hui argued that the chief of the principality should follow in mourning with hempen mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Guan Hui argued that the chief of the principality should follow in mourning with hempen mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 四年，掌凶禮嚴植之定《儀注》，以亡月遇閏，後年中祥，疑所附月。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Yan Zhizhi, in charge of inauspicious rites, fixed the Ritual Regulations; when the month of death fell in an intercalary month, the second-year xiang mourning raised the question of which month it attached to.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Yan Zhizhi, superintendent of inauspicious rites, finalized the Ritual Regulations; when death occurred in an intercalary month, the xiang mourning in the second year raised the question of which month it should attach to.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「閏蓋餘分，月節則各有所隸。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The intercalary month is a surplus fraction; each month's seasonal node has its own affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The intercalary month is a surplus fraction; each month's seasonal node belongs to its own month.

sentences.zh: 若節屬前月，則宜以前月為忌，節屬後月，則宜以後月為忌。

translations.literal: If the node belongs to the preceding month, then the preceding month should be taken as the anniversary; if the node belongs to the following month, then the following month should be taken as the anniversary.
translations.idiomatic: If the seasonal node belongs to the preceding month, the anniversary should be observed in the preceding month; if it belongs to the following month, the anniversary should be observed in the following month.

sentences.zh: 祥逢閏則宜取遠日。」

translations.literal: When xiang mourning falls in an intercalary month, the more distant date should be taken."
translations.idiomatic: When xiang mourning coincides with an intercalary month, the more distant date should be chosen."

sentences.zh: 又四年，安成國刺稱：「廟新建，欲克今日遷立所生吳太妃神主。

translations.literal: Also in the fourth year, the governor of Ancheng Principality reported: "The temple is newly built; we wish to fix today for moving and installing the spirit tablet of the Prince's birth mother, Grand Consort Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Also in the fourth year, the governor of Ancheng Principality reported: "The temple is newly built, and we wish to set today for moving and installing the spirit tablet of the prince's birth mother, Grand Consort Wu.

sentences.zh: 國王既有妃喪，欲使臣下代祭。

translations.literal: Since the prince is in mourning for his consort, he wishes to have his subordinates perform the sacrifice in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Since the prince is in mourning for his consort, he wishes to have his subordinates perform the sacrifice on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 」明山賓議，以為：「不可。

translations.literal: " Ming Shanbin argued that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Shanbin argued that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 宜待王妃服竟，親奉盛禮。」

translations.literal: One should wait until the princess consort's mourning is complete and then personally perform the full rite."
translations.idiomatic: He held that one should wait until the princess consort's mourning was complete and then personally perform the full ceremony."

sentences.zh: 五年，貴嬪母車喪，議者疑其儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the honored consort's mother died in a carriage accident, and those debating the rite were uncertain of the proper procedure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the honored consort's mother died in a carriage accident, and those debating the rite were uncertain of the proper procedure.

sentences.zh: 明山賓以為：「貴嬪既居母憂，皇太子出貴嬪別第，一舉哀，以申聖情，庶不乖禮。

translations.literal: Ming Shanbin held that: "Since the honored consort is in mourning for her mother, the crown prince should go to the honored consort's separate residence and perform one session of lamentation, to express the sage's feeling; this would presumably not violate ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Shanbin held that since the honored consort was in mourning for her mother, the crown prince should go to the honored consort's separate residence and perform one session of lamentation to express imperial sympathy, which would presumably not violate ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this.

sentences.zh: 又五年，祠部郎司馬褧牒：「貴嬪母車亡，應有服制」，謂「宜准公子為母麻衣之制，既葬而除」。

translations.literal: Also in the fifth year, Sima Jiong, Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Section, submitted: "The honored consort's mother died in a carriage accident and there should be mourning garments," saying "It should follow the regulation for a prince mourning his mother in hempen garments, removed after burial."
translations.idiomatic: Also in the fifth year, Sima Jiong, Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Section, submitted: "The honored consort's mother died in a carriage accident and mourning garments are required," proposing that "It should follow the regulation for a prince mourning his mother in hempen garments, to be removed after burial."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this.

sentences.zh: 六年，申明葬制，凡墓不得造石人獸碑，唯聽作石柱，記名位而已。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, burial regulations were clarified: tombs must not have stone human figures, animal sculptures, or steles; only stone pillars recording name and rank were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, burial regulations were clarified: tombs must not have stone human figures, animal sculptures, or steles; only stone pillars recording name and rank were permitted.

sentences.zh: 七年，安成王慈太妃喪，周舍牒：「使安成、始興諸王以成服日一日為位受吊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when Grand Consort Ci of the Prince of Ancheng died, Zhou She submitted: "Have the princes of Ancheng and Shixing take one day on the day of assuming formal mourning garments to receive condolences in their positions.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Grand Consort Ci of the Prince of Ancheng died, Zhou She submitted: "Have the princes of Ancheng and Shixing set aside one day on the day of assuming formal mourning garments to receive condolences in their positions.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「喪無二主。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In mourning there cannot be two masters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In mourning there cannot be two masters of the rites.

sentences.zh: 二王既在遠，嗣子宜祭攝事。

translations.literal: Since the two princes are far away, the heir should perform the sacrifice and manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the two princes are far away, the heir should perform the sacrifice and manage affairs on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 」周舍牒：「嗣子著細布衣、絹領帶。

translations.literal: " Zhou She submitted: "The heir should wear fine cloth garments with silk collar and belt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She submitted: "The heir should wear fine cloth garments with silk collar and belt.

sentences.zh: 單衣用十五升葛。

translations.literal: The unlined garment should use fifteen-sheng hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The unlined garment should use fifteen-sheng hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 凡有事及歲時節朔望，並於靈所朝夕哭。

translations.literal: For all occasions and at the new and full moon of each month and seasonal festivals, morning and evening lamentation should be performed at the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: For all occasions and at the new and full moon of each month and seasonal festivals, morning and evening lamentation should be performed at the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 三年不聽樂。」

translations.literal: For three years music should not be heard."
translations.idiomatic: For three years music should not be heard."

sentences.zh: 十四年，舍人硃異議：「《禮》，年雖未及成人，已有爵命者，則不為殤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Attendant Zhu Yi argued: "The Rites say that although the age has not yet reached adulthood, if one already holds a noble rank and appointment, one is not treated as a shang death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Attendant Zhu Yi argued: "The Rites state that although one has not yet reached adulthood, if one already holds a noble rank and appointment, one is not treated as a shang death.

sentences.zh: 封陽侯年雖中殤，已有拜封，不應殤服。

translations.literal: Although the Marquis of Fengyang was within middle shang age, he had already received enfeoffment and should not wear shang mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Marquis of Fengyang was within middle shang age, he had already received enfeoffment and should not wear shang mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved this.

sentences.zh: 於是諸王服封陽侯依成人之服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princes wore mourning for the Marquis of Fengyang according to adult mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the princes wore mourning for the Marquis of Fengyang according to adult mourning regulations.

sentences.zh: 大同六年，皇太子啟：「謹案下殤之小功，不行婚冠嫁三嘉之禮，則降服之大功，理不得有三嘉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong, the crown prince submitted: "Respectfully examining lower shang lesser mourning, the three auspicious rites of marriage, capping, and betrothal are not performed; then for reduced mourning of great mourning, by principle the three auspicious rites should not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 6 (540), the crown prince submitted: "On careful examination, for lower shang lesser mourning the three auspicious rites of marriage, capping, and betrothal are not performed; therefore for mourning reduced from one period to great mourning, the three auspicious rites should by principle not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 今行三嘉之禮，竊有小疑。

translations.literal: Now that the three auspicious rites are being performed, I have a small doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the three auspicious rites are being performed, I have some doubt.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「《禮》雲：'大功之末，可以冠子。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The Rites say: 'At the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Rites state: 'At the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son.

sentences.zh: 父小功之末，可以冠子、嫁子、娶婦。

translations.literal: At the end of one's father's lesser mourning, one may cap one's son, marry off one's daughter, and take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of one's father's lesser mourning, one may cap one's son, marry off one's daughter, and take a wife.

sentences.zh: 己雖小功，既卒哭，可以冠、娶妻。

translations.literal: Although one oneself is in lesser mourning, after the end of wailing one may cap oneself and take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: Although one oneself is in lesser mourning, after the end of wailing one may cap oneself and take a wife.

sentences.zh: 下殤之小功則不可。

translations.literal: For lower shang lesser mourning this is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For lower shang lesser mourning this is not permitted.

sentences.zh: '晉代蔡謨、謝沈、丁纂、馮懷等遂雲：'降服大功，可以嫁女。

translations.literal: ' In the Jin era Cai Mo, Xie Shen, Ding Zuan, Feng Huai and others then said: 'Reduced mourning of great mourning permits marrying off a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin era, Cai Mo, Xie Shen, Ding Zuan, Feng Huai, and others then said: 'Reduced mourning of great mourning permits marrying off a daughter.

sentences.zh: '宋代裴松之、何承天又雲：'女有大功之服，亦得出嫁。

translations.literal: ' In the Song era Pei Songzhi and He Chengtian again said: 'A daughter in great mourning may also be married off.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song era, Pei Songzhi and He Chengtian again said: 'A daughter in great mourning may also be married off.

sentences.zh: '范堅、荀伯子等，雖複率意致難，亦未能折。

translations.literal: ' Fan Jian, Xun Bozi and others, although again raising objections according to their own inclinations, were also unable to refute it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jian, Xun Bozi, and others, although again raising objections according to their own inclinations, were also unable to refute this.

sentences.zh: 太始六年，虞和立議：'大功之末，乃可娶婦。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, Yu He established the argument: 'At the end of great mourning, one may take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 6 (270), Yu He established the argument: 'At the end of great mourning, one may take a wife.

sentences.zh: '于時博詢，鹹同和議。

translations.literal: ' At that time on broad consultation, all agreed with He's argument.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, on broad consultation, all agreed with He's argument.

sentences.zh: 齊永明十一年，有大司馬長子之喪，武帝子女同服大功。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming of Qi, when the Grand Marshal's eldest son died, Emperor Wu's sons and daughters wore the same great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming 11 (493), when the Grand Marshal's eldest son died, Emperor Wu's sons and daughters wore the same great mourning.

sentences.zh: 左丞顧杲之議雲：'大功之末，非直皇女嬪降無疑，皇子娉納，亦在非硋。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Gu Guozhi argued: 'At the end of great mourning, it is not only that imperial daughters and consorts reduced in rank are without doubt; princes taking brides is also not prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Gu Guozhi argued: 'At the end of great mourning, it is not only that imperial daughters and consorts reduced in rank are without doubt permitted to marry; princes taking brides is also not prohibited.

sentences.zh: '凡此諸議，皆是公背正文，務為通耳。

translations.literal: ' All these arguments go against the main text for the sake of convenience.
translations.idiomatic: All these arguments depart from the main text of the Rites for the sake of convenience.

sentences.zh: 徐爰、王文憲並雲：'期服降為大功，皆不可以婚嫁。

translations.literal: Xu Ai and Wang Wenhuan both said: 'One-period mourning reduced to great mourning may not marry or give in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai and Wang Wenhuan both said: 'One-period mourning reduced to great mourning may not permit marriage or betrothal.

sentences.zh: '於義乃為不乖，而又不釋其意。

translations.literal: ' In principle this does not violate ritual, yet they also do not explain their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In principle this does not violate ritual, yet they also fail to explain their reasoning.

sentences.zh: 天監十年，信安公主當出適，而有臨川長子大功之慘，具論此義，粗已詳悉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianjian, when Princess Xin'an was to be married off, there was the grief of great mourning for the eldest son of Linchuan; this principle was fully discussed and was already detailed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 10 (511), when Princess Xin'an was to be married off, there was the grief of great mourning for the eldest son of Linchuan; this principle was fully discussed and already set forth in detail.

sentences.zh: 太子今又啟審大功之末乃下殤之小功行婚冠嫁三吉之事。

translations.literal: The crown prince now again submits to examine performing the three auspicious rites of marriage, capping, and betrothal at the end of great mourning, which is lower shang lesser mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince now again submits to examine performing the three auspicious rites of marriage, capping, and betrothal at the end of great mourning—which is lower shang lesser mourning.

sentences.zh: 案《禮》所言下殤小功，本是期服，故不得有三吉之禮。

translations.literal: Examining what the Rites say about lower shang lesser mourning, it was originally one-period mourning, so the three auspicious rites are not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Examining what the Rites say about lower shang lesser mourning, it was originally one-period mourning, so the three auspicious rites are not permitted.

sentences.zh: 況本服是期，降為大功，理當不可。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the original mourning is one period reduced to great mourning, by principle it should not be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the original mourning is one period reduced to great mourning, by principle it should not be permitted.

sentences.zh: 人間行者，是用鄭玄逆降之義。

translations.literal: What people in the world practice uses Zheng Xuan's doctrine of inverse reduction.
translations.idiomatic: What people in the world practice follows Zheng Xuan's doctrine of inverse reduction.

sentences.zh: 《雜記》雲：'大功之末，可以冠子嫁子。

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Record says: 'At the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Record says: 'At the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter.

sentences.zh: '此謂本服大功，子則小功，逾月以後，於情差輕，所以許有冠嫁。

translations.literal: ' This refers to when one's own mourning is great mourning and one's son is in lesser mourning; after the month has passed, the emotional weight is somewhat lighter, so capping and marriage are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to when one's own mourning is great mourning and one's son is in lesser mourning; after the month has passed, the emotional weight is somewhat lighter, so capping and marriage are permitted.

sentences.zh: 此則小功之末，通得取婦。

translations.literal: This is the end of lesser mourning, when taking a wife is generally permitted.
translations.idiomatic: This is the end of lesser mourning, when taking a wife is generally permitted.

sentences.zh: 前所雲'大功之末，可以冠子嫁子'，此是簡出大功之身，不得取婦。

translations.literal: The earlier statement 'at the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter' selectively extracts the person in great mourning, who may not take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier statement 'at the end of great mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter' selectively addresses the person in great mourning, who may not take a wife.

sentences.zh: 後言'小功之末，可以冠子嫁子'，非直子得冠嫁，亦得取婦。

translations.literal: The later statement 'at the end of lesser mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter' means not only that the son may be capped and married off, but also that one may take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: The later statement 'at the end of lesser mourning, one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter' means not only that the son may be capped and married off, but also that one may take a wife oneself.

sentences.zh: 故有出沒。

translations.literal: Therefore there is variation in what is included and excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore there is variation in what is included and excluded.

sentences.zh: 婚禮國之大典，宜有畫一。

translations.literal: Marriage rites are a great state ceremony and should have uniform standards.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage rites are a great state ceremony and should have uniform standards.

sentences.zh: 今宗室及外戚，不得複輒有幹啟，禮官不得輒為曲議。

translations.literal: Now members of the imperial clan and maternal kin must not again presumptuously submit petitions, and ritual officials must not again make distorted arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth members of the imperial clan and maternal kin must not again presumptuously submit petitions, and ritual officials must not again make distorted arguments.

sentences.zh: 可依此以為法。」

translations.literal: This may be followed as the law."
translations.idiomatic: This may be followed as the law."

sentences.zh: 後齊定令，親王、公主、太妃、妃及從三品已上喪者，借白鼓一面，喪畢進輸。

translations.literal: Later Qi fixed the statute: for mourning of princes, princesses, grand consorts, consorts, and kin of the third rank and above, one white drum was lent; after mourning it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi fixed the statute: for mourning of princes, princesses, grand consorts, consorts, and kin of the third rank and above, one white drum was lent; after mourning it was returned.

sentences.zh: 王、郡公主、太妃、儀同三司已上及令僕，皆聽立凶門柏曆。

translations.literal: Princes, commandery princesses, grand consorts, and those of third-rank-equivalent and above, as well as ministers and vice-ministers, were all permitted to erect mourning gates and cypress barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, commandery princesses, grand consorts, and those of third-rank-equivalent and above, as well as ministers and vice-ministers, were all permitted to erect mourning gates and cypress barriers.

sentences.zh: 三品已上及五等開國，通用方相。

translations.literal: Those of the third rank and above and fifth-rank enfeoffed lords generally used the fangxiang exorcist.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the third rank and above and fifth-rank enfeoffed lords generally used the fangxiang exorcist.

sentences.zh: 四品已下，達于庶人，以魌頭。

translations.literal: From the fourth rank down to commoners, the qi tou mask was used.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth rank down to commoners, the qi tou mask was used.

sentences.zh: 旌則一品九旒，二品、三品七旒，四品、五品五旒，六品、七品三旒，八品已下，達于庶人，唯旐而已。

translations.literal: For banners, the first rank had nine tassels, second and third ranks seven tassels, fourth and fifth ranks five tassels, sixth and seventh ranks three tassels, and from the eighth rank down to commoners, only the pennant.
translations.idiomatic: For funeral banners, the first rank had nine tassels, second and third ranks seven tassels, fourth and fifth ranks five tassels, sixth and seventh ranks three tassels, and from the eighth rank down to commoners, only the pennant.

sentences.zh: 其建旐，三品已上及開國子、男，其長至軫，四品、五品至輪，六品至於九品至較。

translations.literal: For erecting the pennant, for those of the third rank and above and enfeoffed viscounts and barons, its length reached the end of the shaft; for fourth and fifth ranks it reached the wheel; for sixth through ninth ranks it reached the yoke.
translations.idiomatic: For erecting the pennant, for those of the third rank and above and enfeoffed viscounts and barons, its length reached the end of the shaft; for fourth and fifth ranks it reached the wheel; for sixth through ninth ranks it reached the yoke.

sentences.zh: 勳品達于庶人，不過七尺。

translations.literal: For merit ranks down to commoners, the height did not exceed seven chi.
translations.idiomatic: For merit ranks down to commoners, the height did not exceed seven chi.

sentences.zh: 王元軌子欲改葬祖及祖母，列上未知所服。

translations.literal: The son of Wang Yuangui wished to reinter his grandfather and grandmother; those listed above did not know what mourning to wear.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yuangui's son wished to reinter his grandfather and grandmother, the officials listed above did not know what mourning garments to wear.

sentences.zh: 邢子才議曰：「《禮》'改葬緦麻'。

translations.literal: Xing Zicai argued: "The Rites say 'reinterment—hempen mourning.'"
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai argued: "The Rites state, 'For reinterment—hempen mourning.'"

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注：'臣為君，子為父，妻為夫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotated: "A minister for his lord, a son for his father, a wife for her husband."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan annotated: "A minister for his lord, a son for his father, a wife for her husband."

sentences.zh: '唯三人而已。

translations.literal: "Only these three persons."
translations.idiomatic: "Only these three relationships."

sentences.zh: 然嫡曾孫、孫承重者，曾祖父母、祖父母改葬，既並三年之服，皆應服緦。

translations.literal: Yet for a legitimate great-grandson or grandson who bears the mourning obligation, when great-grandparents or grandparents are reinterred, since they already wear three-year mourning, all should wear hempen mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a legitimate great-grandson or grandson who bears the primary mourning obligation, when great-grandparents or grandparents are reinterred, since they already wear three-year mourning, all should wear hempen mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 而止言三人，若非遺漏，便是舉其略耳。」

translations.literal: Yet it mentions only three persons—if this is not an omission, it is merely stating the summary."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the text mentions only three relationships—if this is not an omission, it is merely stating the summary."

sentences.zh: 開皇初，高祖思定典禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Emperor Gaozu wished to fix the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Emperor Gaozu wished to establish the canonical rites.

sentences.zh: 太常卿牛弘奏曰：「聖教陵替，國章殘缺，漢、晉為法，隨俗因時，未足經國庇人，弘風施化。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Niu Hong submitted: "Sacred teaching has declined, state regulations are incomplete; taking Han and Jin as models and adapting to custom and the times is insufficient to govern the state, protect the people, and spread civilizing influence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Niu Hong submitted: "Sacred teaching has declined and state regulations are incomplete; taking Han and Jin as models and adapting to custom and the times is insufficient to govern the state, protect the people, and spread civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 且制禮作樂，事歸元首，江南王儉，偏隅一臣，私撰儀注，多違古法。

translations.literal: Moreover, establishing rites and composing music is the sovereign's prerogative; Wang Jian of Jiangnan, a minister in a remote corner, privately compiled ritual regulations that often violated ancient law.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, establishing rites and composing music is the sovereign's prerogative; Wang Jian of Jiangnan, a minister in a remote corner, privately compiled ritual regulations that often violated ancient law.

sentences.zh: 就廬非東階之位，凶門豈設重之禮？

translations.literal: The mourning hut is not the position of the eastern steps; how can the mourning gate establish the rite of double mourning?
translations.idiomatic: The mourning hut is not the position of the eastern steps; how can the mourning gate establish the rite of double mourning?

sentences.zh: 兩蕭累代，舉國遵行。

translations.literal: The two Xiao dynasties for successive generations had the whole state follow these practices.
translations.idiomatic: The two Xiao dynasties for successive generations had the whole state follow these practices.

sentences.zh: 後魏及齊，風牛本隔，殊不尋究，遙相師祖，故山東之人，浸以成俗。

translations.literal: Later Wei and Qi were fundamentally separate in origin and did not investigate closely, yet transmitted them from afar as models; therefore the people of Shandong gradually made them custom.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei and Qi were fundamentally separate in origin and did not investigate closely, yet transmitted them from afar as models; therefore the people of Shandong gradually made them custom.

sentences.zh: 西魏已降，師旅弗遑，賓嘉之禮，盡未詳定。

translations.literal: From Western Wei onward, with military campaigns unceasing, the rites of guest and celebration were entirely undetermined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From Western Wei onward, with military campaigns unceasing, the rites of guest reception and celebration were entirely undetermined in detail.

sentences.zh: 今休明啟運，憲章伊始，請據前經，革茲俗弊。

translations.literal: Now with enlightened rule beginning and statutes newly established, I request basing on former classics to reform these customary abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Now with enlightened rule beginning and statutes newly established, I request basing on former classics to reform these customary abuses.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「可。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」弘因奏征學者，撰儀禮百卷。

translations.literal: " Hong then submitted requesting scholars be summoned to compile one hundred volumes of Ritual Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then submitted requesting scholars be summoned to compile one hundred volumes of Ritual Regulations.

sentences.zh: 悉用東齊《儀注》以為准，亦微采王儉禮。

translations.literal: All used Eastern Qi Ritual Regulations as the standard, also slightly adopting Wang Jian's rites.
translations.idiomatic: All used Eastern Qi Ritual Regulations as the standard, also slightly adopting Wang Jian's rites.

sentences.zh: 修畢，上之，詔遂班天下，鹹使遵用焉。

translations.literal: When compilation was complete, it was submitted; an edict then promulgated it throughout the realm, and all were made to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: When compilation was complete, it was submitted; an edict then promulgated it throughout the realm, and all were made to follow it.

sentences.zh: 其喪紀，上自王公，下逮庶人，著令皆為定制，無相差越。

translations.literal: For mourning regulations, from princes and dukes down to commoners, fixed statutes were all made uniform custom, with no differences or excesses.
translations.idiomatic: For mourning regulations, from princes and dukes down to commoners, fixed statutes were all made uniform custom, with no differences or excesses.

sentences.zh: 正一品薨，則鴻臚卿監護喪事，司儀令示禮制。

translations.literal: When a first-rank official died, the Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception supervised the funeral, and the Director of Ritual Regulation displayed the ritual system.
translations.idiomatic: When a first-rank official died, the Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception supervised the funeral, and the Director of Ritual Regulation displayed the ritual system.

sentences.zh: 二品已上，則鴻臚丞監護，司儀丞示禮制。

translations.literal: For second rank and above, the Assistant Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception supervised, and the Assistant Director of Ritual Regulation displayed the ritual system.
translations.idiomatic: For second rank and above, the Assistant Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception supervised, and the Assistant Director of Ritual Regulation displayed the ritual system.

sentences.zh: 五品已上薨、卒，及三品已上有期親已上喪，並掌儀一人示禮制。

translations.literal: For fifth rank and above who died, and for third rank and above with mourning for kin within one period and above, one ritual officer was assigned to display the ritual system.
translations.idiomatic: For fifth rank and above who died, and for third rank and above with mourning for kin within one period and above, one ritual officer was assigned to display the ritual system.

sentences.zh: 官人在職喪，聽斂以朝服，有封者，斂以冕服，未有官者，白帢單衣。

translations.literal: For officials who died while in office, they were permitted to be enshrouded in court dress; those with enfeoffment were enshrouded in coronation robes; those without office wore white headcloth and unlined garment.
translations.idiomatic: For officials who died while in office, they were permitted to be enshrouded in court dress; those with enfeoffment were enshrouded in coronation robes; those without office wore white headcloth and unlined garment.

sentences.zh: 婦人有官品者，亦以其服斂。

translations.literal: Women with official rank were also enshrouded in their rank garments.
translations.idiomatic: Women with official rank were also enshrouded in their rank garments.

sentences.zh: 棺內不得置金銀珠寶。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, and jewels must not be placed inside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, and jewels must not be placed inside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 諸重，一品懸鬲六，五品已上四，六品已下二。

translations.literal: For all bell sets, first rank suspended six tripods, fifth rank and above four, sixth rank and below two.
translations.idiomatic: For all bell sets, first rank suspended six tripods, fifth rank and above four, sixth rank and below two.

sentences.zh: 轜車，三品已上油幰，硃絲絡網，施襈，兩箱畫龍，幰竿諸末垂六旒蘇。

translations.literal: For the hearse, third rank and above had oiled canopy, vermilion silk net, applied streamers, both compartments painted with dragons, canopy pole and ornaments hanging six tassel clusters.
translations.idiomatic: For the hearse, third rank and above had oiled canopy, vermilion silk net, applied streamers, both compartments painted with dragons, canopy pole and ornaments hanging six tassel clusters.

sentences.zh: 七品已上油幰，施襈，兩箱畫雲氣，垂四旒蘇。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above had oiled canopy, applied streamers, both compartments painted with cloud patterns, hanging four tassel clusters.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank and above had oiled canopy, applied streamers, both compartments painted with cloud patterns, hanging four tassel clusters.

sentences.zh: 八品已下，達于庶人，鱉甲車，無幰襈旒蘇畫飾。

translations.literal: Eighth rank and below down to commoners used tortoise-shell-pattern carts, without canopy, streamers, tassels, or painted decoration.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth rank and below down to commoners used tortoise-shell-pattern carts, without canopy, streamers, tassels, or painted decoration.

sentences.zh: 執紼，一品五十人，三品已上四十人，四品三十人，並布幘深衣。

translations.literal: For holding the coffin cord, first rank fifty persons, third rank and above forty persons, fourth rank thirty persons, all wearing cloth headcloths and deep garments.
translations.idiomatic: For holding the coffin cord, first rank fifty persons, third rank and above forty persons, fourth rank thirty persons, all wearing cloth headcloths and deep garments.

sentences.zh: 三品已上四引、四披、六鐸、六翣。

translations.literal: Third rank and above had four guides, four canopies, six bells, six feather fans.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above had four guides, four canopies, six bells, six feather fans.

sentences.zh: 五品已上二引、二披、四鐸、四翣。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above had two guides, two canopies, four bells, four feather fans.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above had two guides, two canopies, four bells, four feather fans.

sentences.zh: 九品已上二鐸、二翣。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above had two bells, two feather fans.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank and above had two bells, two feather fans.

sentences.zh: 四品已上用方相，七品已上用魌頭。

translations.literal: Fourth rank and above used the fangxiang exorcist; seventh rank and above used the qi tou mask.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and above used the fangxiang exorcist; seventh rank and above used the qi tou mask.

sentences.zh: 在京師葬者，去城七裏外。

translations.literal: Those buried in the capital were buried seven li outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Those buried in the capital were buried seven li outside the city.

sentences.zh: 三品已上立碑，螭首龜趺。

translations.literal: Third rank and above erected steles with dragon-head cap and tortoise base.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above erected steles with dragon-head cap and tortoise base.

sentences.zh: 趺上高不得過九尺。

translations.literal: The height on the base must not exceed nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: The height on the base must not exceed nine chi.

sentences.zh: 七品已上立碣，高四尺。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and above erected stone tablets, four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank and above erected stone tablets, four chi high.

sentences.zh: 圭首方趺。

translations.literal: With gui-shaped top and square base.
translations.idiomatic: With gui-shaped top and square base.

sentences.zh: 若隱淪道素，孝義著聞者，雖無爵，奏，聽立碣。

translations.literal: If one lived in seclusion with plain virtue and filial piety and righteousness were renowned, although without rank, on memorial submission permission was granted to erect a tablet.
translations.idiomatic: If one lived in seclusion with plain virtue and filial piety and righteousness were renowned, although without rank, on memorial submission permission was granted to erect a tablet.

sentences.zh: 三年及期喪，不數閏。

translations.literal: For three-year and one-period mourning, intercalary months were not counted.
translations.idiomatic: For three-year and one-period mourning, intercalary months were not counted.

sentences.zh: 大功已下數之。

translations.literal: For great mourning and below they were counted.
translations.idiomatic: For great mourning and below they were counted.

sentences.zh: 以閏月亡者，祥及忌日，皆以閏所附之月為正。

translations.literal: When death occurred in an intercalary month, for xiang mourning and anniversary days, the month to which the intercalary month was attached was taken as correct.
translations.idiomatic: When death occurred in an intercalary month, for xiang mourning and anniversary days, the month to which the intercalary month was attached was taken as correct.

sentences.zh: 凶服不入公門。

translations.literal: Mourning garments did not enter the public gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garments did not enter the public gate.

sentences.zh: 期喪已下不解官者，在外曹礻聶緣紗帽。

translations.literal: For one-period mourning and below without leaving office, in the outer office they wore gauze caps with twisted borders.
translations.idiomatic: For one-period mourning and below without leaving office, in the outer office they wore gauze caps with twisted borders.

sentences.zh: 若重喪被起者，皁絹下裙帽。

translations.literal: If recalled from double mourning, they wore black silk lower skirt and cap.
translations.idiomatic: If recalled from double mourning, they wore black silk lower skirt and cap.

sentences.zh: 若入宮殿及須朝見者，冠服依百官例。

translations.literal: If entering the palace hall or needing to attend court audience, cap and garments followed the example of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: If entering the palace hall or needing to attend court audience, cap and garments followed the example of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 齊衰心喪已上，雖有奪情，並終喪不吊不賀不預宴。

translations.literal: For qi mourning and heart-mourning and above, although there was dispensation from mourning, throughout the mourning period they did not offer condolences, did not offer congratulations, and did not attend banquets.
translations.idiomatic: For qi mourning and heart-mourning and above, although there was dispensation from mourning, throughout the mourning period they did not offer condolences, did not offer congratulations, and did not attend banquets.

sentences.zh: 期喪未練，大功未葬，不吊不賀，並終喪不預宴。

translations.literal: One-period mourning before lian, great mourning before burial—no condolences or congratulations, and throughout mourning no banquets.
translations.idiomatic: One-period mourning before lian, great mourning before burial—no condolences or congratulations, and throughout mourning no banquets.

sentences.zh: 小功已下，假滿依例。

translations.literal: Lesser mourning and below, when leave was complete followed the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser mourning and below, when leave was complete followed the regulation.

sentences.zh: 居五服之喪，受冊及之職，儀衛依常式，唯鼓樂從而不作。

translations.literal: While in mourning within the five degrees, upon receiving appointment and taking office, ceremonial guards followed the usual form, only drums and music followed but were not played.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning within the five degrees, upon receiving appointment and taking office, ceremonial guards followed the usual form, only drums and music followed but were not played.

sentences.zh: 若以戎事，不用此制。

translations.literal: If for military affairs, this regulation was not used.
translations.idiomatic: If for military affairs, this regulation was not used.

sentences.zh: 自秦兼天下，朝覲之禮遂廢。

translations.literal: From when Qin united the realm, the rite of court audience was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From when Qin united the realm, the rite of court audience was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及周封蕭詧為梁王，訖于隋，恆稱籓國，始有朝見之儀。

translations.literal: When Zhou enfeoffed Xiao Cha as Prince of Liang, until Sui they constantly called themselves vassal states, and only then were there rites of court audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou enfeoffed Xiao Cha as Prince of Liang, until Sui they constantly called themselves vassal states, and only then were there rites of court audience.

sentences.zh: 梁王之朝周，入畿，大塚宰命有司致積。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang attended court at Zhou, upon entering the capital district, the Grand Minister of Works ordered the officials to present provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang attended court at Zhou, upon entering the capital district, the Grand Minister of Works ordered the officials to present provisions.

sentences.zh: 其餼五牢，米九十筥，皞醢各三十五甕，酒十八壺，米禾各五十車，薪芻各百車。

translations.literal: The provisions were five sets of sacrificial animals, ninety bins of rice, thirty-five jars each of white and red pickled meat, eighteen pots of wine, fifty carts each of grain and millet, one hundred carts each of firewood and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The provisions were five sets of sacrificial animals, ninety bins of rice, thirty-five jars each of white and red pickled meat, eighteen pots of wine, fifty carts each of grain and millet, one hundred carts each of firewood and fodder.

sentences.zh: 既至，大司空設九儐以致館。

translations.literal: Upon arrival, the Minister of Works set up nine attendants to escort to the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival, the Minister of Works set up nine attendants to escort to the guest house.

sentences.zh: 梁王束帛乘馬，設九介以待之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang brought silk and horses, set up nine attendants to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang brought silk and horses, set up nine attendants to await them.

sentences.zh: 禮成而出。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete they departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete they departed.

sentences.zh: 明日，王朝，受享於廟。

translations.literal: The next day, the prince attended court and received offerings at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the prince attended court and received offerings at the temple.

sentences.zh: 既致享，大塚宰又命公一人，玄冕乘車，陳九儐，以束帛乘馬，致食於賓及賓之從各有差。

translations.literal: After offerings were presented, the Grand Minister of Works again ordered one duke, wearing dark robes and riding in a carriage, to set up nine attendants with silk and horses to present food to the guest and the guest's followers according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: After offerings were presented, the Grand Minister of Works again ordered one duke, wearing dark robes and riding in a carriage, to set up nine attendants with silk and horses to present food to the guest and the guest's followers according to rank.

sentences.zh: 致食訖，又命公一人，弁服乘車，執贄，設九儐以勞賓。

translations.literal: When food presentation was complete, another duke was ordered, wearing cap and riding in a carriage, holding tribute gifts, to set up nine attendants to welcome the guest.
translations.idiomatic: When food presentation was complete, another duke was ordered, wearing cap and riding in a carriage, holding tribute gifts, to set up nine attendants to welcome the guest.

sentences.zh: 王設九介，迎於門外。

translations.literal: The prince set up nine attendants to welcome outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince set up nine attendants to welcome outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 明日，朝服乘車，還贄於公。

translations.literal: The next day, in court dress riding in a carriage, he returned the tribute gifts to the duke.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, in court dress riding in a carriage, he returned the tribute gifts to the duke.

sentences.zh: 公皮弁迎於大門，授贄受贄，並於堂之中楹。

translations.literal: The duke in leather cap welcomed at the great gate; presenting and receiving tribute gifts both took place at the central pillar of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The duke in leather cap welcomed at the great gate; presenting and receiving tribute gifts both took place at the central pillar of the hall.

sentences.zh: 又明日，王朝服，設九介，乘車，備儀衛，以見於公。

translations.literal: Again the next day, the prince in court dress, setting up nine attendants, riding in a carriage with full ceremonial guard, went to visit the duke.
translations.idiomatic: Again the next day, the prince in court dress, setting up nine attendants, riding in a carriage with full ceremonial guard, went to visit the duke.

sentences.zh: 事畢，公致享。

translations.literal: When affairs were complete, the duke presented offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were complete, the duke presented offerings.

sentences.zh: 明日，三孤一人，又執贄勞于梁王。

translations.literal: The next day, one of the three solitaries again held tribute gifts to welcome the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, one of the three solitaries again held tribute gifts to welcome the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 明日，王還贄。

translations.literal: The next day, the prince returned the tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the prince returned the tribute gifts.

sentences.zh: 又明日，王見三孤，如見三公。

translations.literal: Again the next day, the prince visited the three solitaries, as when visiting the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Again the next day, the prince visited the three solitaries, as when visiting the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 明日，卿一人，又執贄勞王。

translations.literal: The next day, one minister again held tribute gifts to welcome the prince.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, one minister again held tribute gifts to welcome the prince.

sentences.zh: 王見卿，又如三孤。

translations.literal: The prince visited the minister, again as with the three solitaries.
translations.idiomatic: The prince visited the minister, again as with the three solitaries.

sentences.zh: 於是三公、三孤、六卿，又各餼賓，並屬官之長為使。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three dukes, three solitaries, and six ministers each again presented provisions to the guest, with the heads of subordinate offices as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the three dukes, three solitaries, and six ministers each again presented provisions to the guest, with the heads of subordinate offices as envoys.

sentences.zh: 牢米束帛同三公。

translations.literal: Sacrificial animals, rice, and silk were the same as for the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial animals, rice, and silk were the same as for the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年正月，梁主蕭巋朝于京師，次於郊外。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Kaihuang, the Liang ruler Xiao Cong attended court at the capital, stopping at the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaihuang 4 (584), the Liang ruler Xiao Cong attended court at the capital, stopping at the outskirts.

sentences.zh: 詔廣平王楊雄、吏部尚書韋世康持節以迎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Guangping Yang Xiong and Minister of Personnel Wei Shikang to hold credentials and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince of Guangping Yang Xiong and Minister of Personnel Wei Shikang to hold credentials and welcome him.

sentences.zh: 衛尉設次於驛館。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Guard set up a pavilion at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Guard set up a pavilion at the post station.

sentences.zh: 雄等降就便幕。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others descended to the temporary tent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others descended to the temporary tent.

sentences.zh: 巋服通天冠、絳紗袍、端珽，立於東階下，西面。

translations.literal: Cong wore the tongtian cap, crimson gauze robe, and duan yi, standing below the eastern steps, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wore the tongtian cap, crimson gauze robe, and duan yi, standing below the eastern steps, facing west.

sentences.zh: 文武陪侍，如其國。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials attended, as in his state.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials attended, as in his state.

sentences.zh: 雄等立於門右，東面。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others stood to the right of the gate, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others stood to the right of the gate, facing east.

sentences.zh: 巋攝內史令柳顧言出門請事。

translations.literal: Cong, acting as Director of the Secretariat, Liu Guyuan went out the gate to inquire of the business.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, acting as Director of the Secretariat, Liu Guyuan went out the gate to inquire of the business.

sentences.zh: 世康曰：「奉詔勞于梁帝。

translations.literal: Shikang said: "By edict I welcome the Liang Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang said: "By edict I welcome the Liang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」顧言入告。

translations.literal: " Guyuan entered to report.
translations.idiomatic: Guyuan entered to report.

sentences.zh: 巋出，迎於館門之外，西面再拜。

translations.literal: Cong went out and welcomed outside the station gate, facing west and bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: Cong went out and welcomed outside the station gate, facing west and bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 持節者導雄與巋俱入，至於庭下。

translations.literal: The credential holders guided Xiong and Cong together inside, reaching below the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The credential holders guided Xiong and Cong together inside, reaching below the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 巋北面再拜受詔訖。

translations.literal: Cong faced north and bowed twice to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Cong faced north and bowed twice to receive the edict.

sentences.zh: 雄等乃出，立於館門外道右東向。

translations.literal: Xiong and the others then went out and stood to the right outside the station gate, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and the others then went out and stood to the right outside the station gate, facing east.

sentences.zh: 巋送於門外，西面再拜。

translations.literal: Cong escorted them to outside the gate, facing west and bowing twice.
translations.idiomatic: Cong escorted them to outside the gate, facing west and bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 及奉見，高祖冠通天冠，服絳紗袍，禦大興殿，如朝儀。

translations.literal: When he had audience, Emperor Gaozu wore the tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, presiding at Daxing Hall, as in court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When he had audience, Emperor Gaozu wore the tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, presiding at Daxing Hall, as in court ritual.

sentences.zh: 巋服遠遊冠，朝服以入，君臣並拜，禮畢而出。

translations.literal: Cong wore the yuanyou cap and court dress to enter; lord and ministers all bowed, and when the rite was complete they departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wore the yuanyou cap and court dress to enter; lord and ministers all bowed, and when the rite was complete they departed.

sentences.zh: 古者天子征伐，則宜於社，造于祖，類於上帝。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven went on campaign, he performed the yi rite at the altar of soil, the zao rite at the ancestral temple, and the lei rite to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven went on campaign, he performed the yi rite at the altar of soil, the zao rite at the ancestral temple, and the lei rite to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 還亦以牲遍告。

translations.literal: On return also sacrificial victims were used to announce everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: On return also sacrificial victims were used to announce everywhere.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，陸璉議定軍禮，遵其制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang, Lu Lian discussed and fixed military rites, following this system.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Liang Tianjian, Lu Lian discussed and fixed military rites, following this system.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「宜者請征討之宜，造者稟謀於廟，類者奉天時以明伐，並明不敢自專。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yi means seeking the propriety of campaign and attack; zao means receiving counsel at the temple; lei means following heaven's seasons to clarify the campaign—all show that one dare not act on one's own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yi means seeking the propriety of campaign and attack; zao means receiving counsel at the temple; lei means following heaven's seasons to clarify the campaign—all show that one dare not act on one's own.

sentences.zh: 陳幣承命可也。

translations.literal: Presenting silks to receive the mandate is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting silks to receive the mandate is sufficient.

sentences.zh: 」璉不能對。

translations.literal: " Lian could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lian could not reply.

sentences.zh: 嚴植之又爭之，於是告用牲幣，反亦如之。

translations.literal: Yan Zhizhi again disputed it; thereupon announcement used sacrificial victims and silks, and return was also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhizhi again disputed it; thereupon announcement used sacrificial victims and silks, and return was also the same.

sentences.zh: 後齊天子親征纂嚴，則服通天冠，文物充庭。

translations.literal: Later Qi when the Son of Heaven personally went on campaign to assemble the army, he wore the tongtian cap and ceremonial objects filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi when the Son of Heaven personally went on campaign to assemble the army, he wore the tongtian cap and ceremonial objects filled the court.

sentences.zh: 有司奏更衣，乃入，冠武弁，弁左貂附蟬以出。

translations.literal: When the relevant office reported changing garments, he entered, put on the military cap, with sable on the left and cicada ornament attached, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: When the relevant office reported changing garments, he entered, put on the military cap with sable on the left and cicada ornament attached, and went out.

sentences.zh: 誓訖，擇日備法駕，乘木輅，以選於廟。

translations.literal: When the oath was complete, an auspicious day was chosen to prepare the imperial carriage, ride the wooden chariot, and proceed to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the oath was complete, an auspicious day was chosen to prepare the imperial carriage, ride the wooden chariot, and proceed to the temple.

sentences.zh: 載遷廟主于齋車，以俟行。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of the moved temple were loaded on the fasting carriage to await departure.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets of the moved temple were loaded on the fasting carriage to await departure.

sentences.zh: 次宜於社，有司以毛血釁軍鼓，載帝社石主于車，以俟行。

translations.literal: Next the yi rite was performed at the altar of soil; the relevant office used fur and blood to anoint the military drums, and the spirit stone of the imperial altar of soil was loaded on a carriage to await departure.
translations.idiomatic: Next the yi rite was performed at the altar of soil; the relevant office used fur and blood to anoint the military drums, and the spirit stone of the imperial altar of soil was loaded on a carriage to await departure.

sentences.zh: 次擇日陳六軍，備大駕，類於上帝。

translations.literal: Next an auspicious day was chosen to array the six armies, prepare the grand carriage, and perform the lei rite to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Next an auspicious day was chosen to array the six armies, prepare the grand carriage, and perform the lei rite to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 次擇日祈後土、神州、嶽鎮、海瀆、源川等。

translations.literal: Next an auspicious day was chosen to pray to the Queen of Earth, the Spirit of the Land, mountains, commanderies, seas, rivers, and source streams.
translations.idiomatic: Next an auspicious day was chosen to pray to the Queen of Earth, the Spirit of the Land, mountains, commanderies, seas, rivers, and source streams.

sentences.zh: 乃為坎盟，督將列牲于坎南，北首。

translations.literal: Then a pit covenant was made; supervising generals arranged victims south of the pit, heads facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Then a pit covenant was made; supervising generals arranged victims south of the pit, heads facing north.

sentences.zh: 有司坎前讀盟文，割牲耳，承血。

translations.literal: The relevant office read the covenant text before the pit and cut off the victims' ears, receiving the blood.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office read the covenant text before the pit and cut off the victims' ears, receiving the blood.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受牲耳，遍授大將，乃置於坎。

translations.literal: The emperor received the victims' ears and passed them in turn to the grand generals, then placed them in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the victims' ears and passed them in turn to the grand generals, then placed them in the pit.

sentences.zh: 又歃血，歃遍，又以置坎。

translations.literal: Blood was also tasted; after all had tasted, it was again placed in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: Blood was also tasted; after all had tasted, it was again placed in the pit.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，埋牲及盟書。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the victims and covenant text were buried.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the victims and covenant text were buried.

sentences.zh: 又卜日，建牙旗于鹆單，祭乙太牢，及所過名山大川，使有司致祭。

translations.literal: Again on a chosen day, the military banner was erected at Yuodan; a full complement of sacrificial animals was offered to Yi, and at famous mountains and great rivers passed along the route, the relevant office performed sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Again on a chosen day, the military banner was erected at Yuodan; a full complement of sacrificial animals was offered to Yi, and at famous mountains and great rivers passed along the route, the relevant office performed sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 將屆戰所，卜剛日，備玄牲，列軍容，設柴於辰地，為墠而祃祭。

translations.literal: When approaching the battlefield, on a yang day a black victim was prepared, the army array was set, firewood was arranged at the chen position, an altar was made and the ma sacrifice performed.
translations.idiomatic: When approaching the battlefield, on a yang day a black victim was prepared, the army array was set, firewood was arranged at the chen position, an altar was made and the ma sacrifice performed.

sentences.zh: 大司馬奠矢，有司奠毛血，樂奏《大護》之音。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal presented arrows; the relevant office presented fur and blood; music played the melody "Great Protection."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal presented arrows; the relevant office presented fur and blood; music played the melody "Great Protection."

sentences.zh: 禮畢，徹牲，柴燎。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the victims were removed and the firewood burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the victims were removed and the firewood burned.

sentences.zh: 戰前一日，皇帝禱祖，司空禱社。

translations.literal: One day before battle, the emperor prayed to the ancestors; the Minister of Works prayed at the altar of soil.
translations.idiomatic: One day before battle, the emperor prayed to the ancestors; the Minister of Works prayed at the altar of soil.

sentences.zh: 戰勝則各報乙太牢。

translations.literal: If victorious, each reported with a full complement of sacrificial animals to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: If victorious, each reported with a full complement of sacrificial animals to Yi.

sentences.zh: 又乙太牢賞用命戰士于祖，引功臣入旌門，即神庭而授版焉。

translations.literal: Again with a full complement of sacrificial animals the meritorious warriors who obeyed orders in battle were rewarded at the ancestral temple; meritorious ministers were led through the banner gate and received their tablets at the spirit hall.
translations.idiomatic: Again with a full complement of sacrificial animals the meritorious warriors who obeyed orders in battle were rewarded at the ancestral temple; meritorious ministers were led through the banner gate and received their tablets at the spirit hall.

sentences.zh: 又罰不用命於社，即神庭行戮訖，振旅而還。

translations.literal: Again those who disobeyed orders were punished at the altar of soil; execution was carried out at the spirit hall, and when complete the army was rallied and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Again those who disobeyed orders were punished at the altar of soil; execution was carried out at the spirit hall, and when complete the army was rallied and returned.

sentences.zh: 格廟詣社訖，擇日行飲至禮，文物充庭。

translations.literal: After arriving at the temple and completing the rite at the altar of soil, an auspicious day was chosen for the drink-on-return rite, with ceremonial objects filling the court.
translations.idiomatic: After arriving at the temple and completing the rite at the altar of soil, an auspicious day was chosen for the drink-on-return rite, with ceremonial objects filling the court.

sentences.zh: 有司執簡，紀年號月朔，陳六師凱入格廟之事，飲至策勳之美，因述其功，不替賞典焉。

translations.literal: The relevant office held bamboo slips recording the year, month, and new moon, stating the six armies' triumphant entry at the temple, the beauty of the drink-on-return and recording of merit, thereby recounting their achievements without omitting the reward canon.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office held bamboo slips recording the year, month, and new moon, stating the six armies' triumphant entry at the temple, the beauty of the drink-on-return and recording of merit, thereby recounting their achievements without omitting the reward canon.

sentences.zh: 隋制，行幸所過名山大川，則有司致祭。

translations.literal: Under Sui regulations, at famous mountains and great rivers passed during imperial progress, the relevant office performed sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui regulations, at famous mountains and great rivers passed during imperial progress, the relevant office performed sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嶽瀆乙太牢，山川以少牢。

translations.literal: For mountains and rivers a full complement of sacrificial animals; for mountains and streams a lesser complement.
translations.idiomatic: For mountains and rivers a full complement of sacrificial animals; for mountains and streams a lesser complement.

sentences.zh: 親征及巡狩，則類上帝、宜社、造廟，還禮亦如之，將發軔，則「Ｑ祭。

translations.literal: On personal campaign and imperial tour, the lei rite to the Supreme Lord, yi at the altar of soil, and zao at the temple were performed; return rites were also the same; before setting out, the she sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: On personal campaign and imperial tour, the lei rite to the Supreme Lord, yi at the altar of soil, and zao at the temple were performed; return rites were also the same; before setting out, the she sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 其禮，有司於國門外委土為山象，設埋坎。

translations.literal: For this rite, the relevant office piled earth outside the state gate into a mountain image and set up a burial pit.
translations.idiomatic: For this rite, the relevant office piled earth outside the state gate into a mountain image and set up a burial pit.

sentences.zh: 有司刳羊，陳俎豆。

translations.literal: The relevant office slaughtered a sheep and set out trays and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office slaughtered a sheep and set out trays and vessels.

sentences.zh: 駕將至，委奠幣，薦脯醢，加羊於「Ｑ，西首。

translations.literal: When the carriage was about to arrive, silks were placed as offerings, dried meat and pickled meat presented, and the sheep added to the she altar, head facing west.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage was about to arrive, silks were placed as offerings, dried meat and pickled meat presented, and the sheep added to the she altar, head facing west.

sentences.zh: 又奠酒解羊，並饌埋於坎。

translations.literal: Wine was again offered and the sheep dismembered, and all provisions were buried in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was again offered and the sheep dismembered, and all provisions were buried in the pit.

sentences.zh: 駕至，太僕祭兩軹及軌前，乃飲，授爵，遂轢「Ｑ上而行。

translations.literal: When the carriage arrived, the Grand Master of the Household sacrificed at both wheel hubs and before the track, then drank, received the cup, and rolled over the she altar before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage arrived, the Grand Master of the Household sacrificed at both wheel hubs and before the track, then drank, received the cup, and rolled over the she altar before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，征遼東，煬帝遣諸將于薊城南桑乾河上築社稷二壇，設方壝，行宜社禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye, campaigning against Liaodong, Emperor Yang dispatched the generals south of Ji city on the Sanggan River to build two altars of soil and grain, set up a square enclosure, and perform the yi rite at the altar of soil.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 7 (611), campaigning against Liaodong, Emperor Yang dispatched the generals south of Ji city on the Sanggan River to build two altars of soil and grain, set up a square enclosure, and perform the yi rite at the altar of soil.

sentences.zh: 帝齋于臨朔宮懷荒殿，預告官及侍從各齋于其所。

translations.literal: The emperor fasted at Huaihuang Hall in Linshuo Palace; officials and attendants each fasted at their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fasted at Huaihuang Hall in Linshuo Palace; officials and attendants each fasted at their posts.

sentences.zh: 十二衛士並齋。

translations.literal: The twelve guards all fasted.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve guards all fasted.

sentences.zh: 帝袞冕玉輅，備法駕。

translations.literal: The emperor wore coronation robes and jade chariot, with full imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore coronation robes and jade chariot, with full imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，禦金輅，服通天冠，還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he rode the gold chariot, wore the tongtian cap, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, he rode the gold chariot, wore the tongtian cap, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 又于宮南類上帝，積柴於燎壇，設高祖位於東方。

translations.literal: Again south of the palace the lei rite to the Supreme Lord was performed; firewood was piled on the burning altar, and the Founding Ancestor's seat was set in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Again south of the palace the lei rite to the Supreme Lord was performed; firewood was piled on the burning altar, and the Founding Ancestor's seat was set in the east.

sentences.zh: 帝服大裘以冕，乘玉輅，祭奠玉帛，並如宜社。

translations.literal: The emperor wore great fur robe and coronation cap, rode the jade chariot, and offered jade and silks, all as at the yi rite at the altar of soil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore great fur robe and coronation cap, rode the jade chariot, and offered jade and silks, all as at the yi rite at the altar of soil.

sentences.zh: 諸軍受胙畢，帝就位，觀燎，乃出。

translations.literal: When all armies had received sacrificial meat, the emperor took his seat, observed the burning, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When all armies had received sacrificial meat, the emperor took his seat, observed the burning, and then departed.

sentences.zh: 又於薊城北設壇，祭馬祖於其上，亦有燎。

translations.literal: Again north of Ji city an altar was set up and the Horse Ancestor sacrificed upon it, also with burning.
